scope_note: Every text-to-speech system that matters in 2026 — hosted APIs, hyperscaler services, open-weights models, on-device engines, realtime speech-to-speech and voice conversion — on the axes that actually decide a project: what it sounds like, what it costs, what hardware it needs, what you are legally allowed to do with it, and where it quietly falls over.
method_note: Compiled from primary sources: vendor pricing and documentation pages, Hugging Face model cards, GitHub repositories, papers and public leaderboards. Azure figures come from the Azure Retail Prices API and AWS figures from the AWS Price List API rather than the pricing pages, which render via JavaScript and show placeholders to scrapers — the reason many published comparisons carry stale Azure numbers. Every pricing, latency and licence claim was re-checked against primary sources by a second pass instructed to refute rather than confirm. Where a figure could not be verified it is marked as such rather than smoothed over.

systems.name: ElevenLabs
systems.cloning: Instant (~1 min) + Professional (30 min+). Own voice only, enforced by a live voice-CAPTCHA.
systems.emotion: Inline audio tags, open-ended vocabulary; dialogue mode
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.best_for: Peak expressivity, dialogue and character work; the broadest ecosystem and SDK coverage.
systems.watch: Most expensive flagship per character. v3 is capped at 5,000 chars per request and is not a realtime model. Trains on your content by default — the opt-out is in account settings and is not retroactive.

systems.name: Cartesia
systems.cloning: Instant at the $5/mo tier; professional at $49/mo
systems.emotion: 54-emotion enum plus speed 0.6–1.5× and volume 0.5–2× — the most granular parameterised control found
systems.runs_on: Cloud; deployable into your own AWS account via SageMaker JumpStart
systems.latency_note: sub-90 ms per Cartesia's docs; ~188 ms P50 independently measured
systems.best_for: Telephony and realtime agents — native μ-law 8 kHz output makes it drop-in for phone lines.
systems.watch: The credit-to-character rate is not published anywhere, so true cost per million characters cannot be computed from primary sources. Concurrency caps at 15 even on the $299 plan. Trains on customer content by default.

systems.name: Deepgram
systems.licence: Proprietary; self-host offered under commercial licence
systems.emotion: None — sells context-aware handling of numbers and dates instead
systems.runs_on: Cloud plus a genuine self-hosted deployment
systems.latency_note: sub-200 ms stated on the product page
systems.best_for: High-volume English contact centres. The best concurrency-per-dollar of any major Western vendor, and a real self-host escape hatch.
systems.watch: Narrowest language coverage of the serious contenders, and no cloning or emotion mechanism at all — rules it out for character or media work.

systems.name: Rime
systems.emotion: Split across models — Coda has the quality, only Mist has pronunciation control and custom pauses
systems.runs_on: Cloud, on-prem or VPC
systems.latency_note: sub-100 ms model plus 25–50 ms network, stated separately
systems.best_for: US contact centres wanting naturalistic conversational American English, with the most honest latency disclosure in the segment.
systems.watch: The pricing page contradicts itself on the starter rate. Arcana sunsets 15 August 2026 with automatic migration to Coda; after that it serves Sinhala only.

systems.name: Hume
systems.cloning: From as little as 15 s of audio; also voice design from a description
systems.emotion: Free-form natural-language acting direction — the only vendor doing this
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.latency_note: ~100 ms (Octave 2); ~200 ms (Octave 1) — verified in Hume's docs
systems.best_for: Character work, audio drama and empathic agents where how a line is said is the product.
systems.watch: Perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence over your input with no opt-out identified — the most aggressive data grant in the segment. Concurrency is 1–30. Max 5,000 chars per utterance.

systems.name: Inworld
systems.cloning: Instant from 5–15 s; also voice design
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.latency_note: P90 under 250 ms (TTS-2), under 130 ms (1.5 Mini) — one of only two vendors publishing a percentile
systems.best_for: Games, NPCs and multilingual agents. Concurrency scales 5 → 500, the widest published range in the segment.
systems.watch: Publishes its own competitive benchmark ranking rivals, so treat its comparative claims as vendor-adjacent.

systems.name: Speechify
systems.emotion: SSML plus explicit emotion control on 3.2, 3.0 and English
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.latency_note: sub-100 ms claimed, no percentile or conditions
systems.best_for: Cheapest premium-tier English at volume, with all-inclusive voice-agent minutes that beat assembling STT + LLM + TTS yourself.
systems.watch: The API still defaults to the legacy simba-english model when you omit the model parameter — naive integrations silently get the oldest and worst model. Set it explicitly.

systems.name: LMNT
systems.licence: Proprietary; commercial licence on all paid tiers
systems.cloning: Unlimited voice clones on every tier, including the free one
systems.emotion: Not published
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.latency_note: Marketed on low latency; no figure published
systems.best_for: Teams needing many distinct cloned voices without per-voice fees.
systems.watch: States "no concurrency or rate limits" on paid tiers — unusual enough to confirm contractually before relying on it.

systems.name: Fish Audio
systems.licence: Commercial hosted service; open lineage is research-licensed
systems.cloning: Zero-shot plus a voice-design endpoint at $0.01 per request
systems.emotion: Inline emotion markers (S1 generation)
systems.languages_note: Not published for the hosted models
systems.runs_on: Cloud; the open-weights lineage is self-hostable
systems.best_for: The cheapest credible per-character rate with genuine pay-as-you-go and no subscription.
systems.watch: Billing is per UTF-8 BYTE, not per character. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Cyrillic and Indic characters take 2–3 bytes each, so a million CJK characters costs $30–45 — a hidden penalty on exactly the languages Fish is strongest in.

systems.name: Camb.ai
systems.emotion: MARS-Instruct offers director-level controls, at roughly 2.2× the credit cost per character
systems.runs_on: Cloud; MARS-Nano is an on-device variant
systems.best_for: Dubbing and localisation into long-tail languages, and live broadcast — verified deployments include Ligue 1, NASCAR, FanCode cricket, MLS and Eurovision Sport.
systems.watch: The credit system obscures cost — the same credit buys 2.2× more MARS-Flash than MARS-Instruct, and no simple per-character rate is published.

systems.name: Typecast
systems.emotion: 7 Smart Emotion presets plus context inference from the text
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.best_for: Korean, Japanese and Vietnamese at native quality — an underserved niche most Western vendors handle poorly. 500+ preset voices.
systems.watch: Expensive per character without a corresponding quality lead in English, and only 6 of the 35+ languages are native-quality.

systems.name: Sarvam
systems.emotion: Pace control 0.5–2.0× only
systems.runs_on: India-hosted cloud
systems.best_for: Any product serving Indian-language users — 11 Indic languages, India data residency, rupee billing and native Hinglish handling, which no Western vendor replicates.
systems.watch: Max input is 2,500 characters per request, the tightest limit in the segment. Streaming is capped at 24 kHz. Pricing pages block automated access, so rates are secondary-sourced.

systems.name: Resemble AI
systems.licence: Commercial hosted; the base Chatterbox model is MIT open weights
systems.cloning: Rapid (10 s) and Professional (10–25 min), billed monthly per voice
systems.emotion: Exaggeration/intensity conditioning; DramaBox for dramatic delivery
systems.runs_on: Cloud; on-premises at Enterprise; open weights run on consumer GPUs
systems.best_for: The only vendor selling neural watermarking and deepfake detection as first-class paid products alongside TTS — the right pick when provenance is a requirement.
systems.watch: Visibly repositioned toward deepfake detection; TTS pricing has been removed from the pricing page entirely.

systems.name: WellSaid Labs
systems.licence: Proprietary; free trial excludes commercial rights
systems.emotion: Distinct voice avatars per style, not a runtime parameter
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.best_for: Regulated enterprise narration and e-learning — 96 kHz output, SSO, seat-based governance and Adobe Premiere integration.
systems.watch: Bills per minute of audio rather than per character, and publishes no API rate at all, so it cannot be compared without a sales conversation.

systems.name: Murf AI
systems.emotion: Style presets per voice in Studio
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.best_for: Corporate e-learning, explainer video and IVR prompts where a large library of polished business-narration voices matters more than expressivity.
systems.watch: API billing is a separate cost centre from a Murf Studio subscription — a Studio plan grants you no API characters, which surprises buyers.

systems.name: Smallest.ai
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: Cloud; dedicated infrastructure at Enterprise
systems.best_for: A single vendor for the whole voice-agent loop with genuinely itemised per-component pricing rather than one opaque blended rate.
systems.watch: No per-character rate is published anywhere, so it cannot be compared against character-billed vendors without deriving one. PII removal is a paid add-on rather than default.

systems.name: Unreal Speech
systems.licence: Hosted service; its pricing page states it is powered by Kokoro
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: Cloud; the underlying model is freely self-hostable
systems.best_for: Bulk cost-dominated work — audiobook drafts, article-to-audio, accessibility readers — where per-character cost is the binding constraint.
systems.watch: If the Kokoro attribution on its own pricing page is accurate, you can self-host the identical Apache-2.0 model for free; the value is purely operational convenience.

systems.name: Voicemaker
systems.licence: Proprietary; free tier is personal use only
systems.emotion: Expressive voice tiers at 4× credit cost, not a parameter you control
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.best_for: Low-budget batch voiceover for video and e-learning where a flat monthly subscription beats metered billing.
systems.watch: The 4× credit multiplier on the good voices makes advertised character allowances misleading — a plan billed as 1,000,000 characters delivers 250,000 if you use the expressive tier.

systems.name: Neuphonic
systems.licence: Mixed — some open models, hosted terms unpublished
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: Cloud, on-premises, and genuinely on-device — 2 CPU threads, no GPU, no network
systems.best_for: Edge, embedded and air-gapped deployments. The only vendor here offering a true offline on-device path with a matching cloud API.
systems.watch: Both pricing URLs return 404 — cost cannot be evaluated without a sales conversation. ~60 M active parameters caps the quality ceiling.

systems.name: PlayHT / PlayAI
systems.emotion: Gone
systems.runs_on: Nothing
systems.best_for: Nothing — listed only as a migration warning.
systems.watch: Acquihired by Meta in July 2025 and permanently deleted on 31 December 2025, taking every customer voice clone with it and no export path. The domain no longer resolves. Any 2026-dated roundup still recommending it was not researched.

systems.name: Azure Neural TTS
systems.cloning: Via Custom Neural Voice or Personal Voice, both Limited Access
systems.emotion: Full SSML — express-as styles and roles, prosody, emphasis, phoneme, lexicon, viseme, background audio
systems.runs_on: Cloud, Docker container, embedded SDK, and disconnected operation
systems.best_for: Highest-volume enterprise TTS, the broadest locale coverage, the richest markup surface anywhere, and the only major hyperscaler path to genuinely air-gapped deployment.
systems.watch: Widely quoted at $16 / 1M — the retail price API returns $15.00 across 35 commercial regions. Per-character billing counts SSML markup. Commitment discounts exclude HD, custom and personal voices.

systems.name: Azure Neural HD
systems.emotion: 60+ named styles plus 6 paralinguistic tags, with automatic style prediction from natural language
systems.runs_on: Cloud only, 7 regions, no container path
systems.best_for: Expressive narration, podcasts and emotionally aware customer service.
systems.watch: Cut from $30 to $22 in March 2026, making it cheaper than Google Chirp 3 HD. But the SSML surface is severely reduced — prosody, emphasis and background audio are gone, and Omni additionally drops break and phoneme.

systems.name: Azure Personal Voice
systems.cloning: Zero-shot, gated behind recorded verbal consent AND biometric speaker verification
systems.emotion: Implicit, with automatic sentence-level language detection
systems.runs_on: Cloud only, in enabled regions
systems.best_for: Consumer and prosumer voice replication at scale where 90+ language cross-lingual output from one short sample matters.
systems.watch: The strongest consent architecture of any commercial vendor — and correspondingly gated. Only customers with a direct Microsoft account team relationship are eligible, and every voice requires a recorded acknowledgement.

systems.name: Google Chirp 3
systems.emotion: ~10 SSML tags synchronously and none at all in streaming
systems.runs_on: Cloud; us and eu endpoints keep data in-continent at rest and in use
systems.best_for: Broad-locale generative TTS with true bidirectional streaming and a genuinely useful perpetual free tier.
systems.watch: SSML is unsupported in streaming mode entirely — if you need pronunciation control in a live agent on Google, you must use a legacy voice or handle it upstream.

systems.name: Google Instant Custom Voice
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from ~10 s plus a 10 s recorded consent statement
systems.emotion: Prompting, pause tags, pace 0.25–2×, experimental IPA
systems.languages_note: en-US keys transfer to 6 other locales
systems.runs_on: Cloud; the voice key is held client-side, not stored on Google's servers
systems.best_for: Per-end-user voice cloning without server-side voice storage, which simplifies retention and deletion.
systems.watch: The most expensive mainstream cloud tier apart from Google Studio. A 10-second scripted consent clip is weak identity proof, and the docs do not state that Google cross-matches it against the reference voice.

systems.name: Google Gemini TTS
systems.emotion: Free-form natural-language prompting; up to 2 speakers with per-speaker direction
systems.runs_on: Cloud; streaming only on the 3.1 preview model
systems.best_for: Podcast and dialogue generation, and any workflow where writing a stage direction in English beats hand-authoring SSML.
systems.watch: No SSML at all, maximum 2 speakers, and no streaming except on one preview model. Token billing makes cost-per-character non-obvious — audio tokens run at 25 per second of audio.

systems.name: Amazon Polly
systems.cloning: No self-service — Brand Voice is a bespoke AWS engagement
systems.emotion: Polly SSML; newscaster style on selected voices
systems.runs_on: Cloud plus GovCloud (Standard and Neural only)
systems.best_for: IVR and high-throughput work. Uniquely, SSML tags are EXCLUDED from the billed character count and generated speech may be cached and replayed free — which drives marginal cost to zero for a finite prompt set.
systems.watch: Throughput drops from 80 TPS on Standard to 8 TPS on Neural, Generative and Long-Form, with async batch at just 1 TPS for the latter two.

systems.name: OpenAI
systems.licence: Proprietary; does not train on API data by default
systems.cloning: None — Voice Engine never shipped broadly
systems.emotion: Free-form instructions field controlling accent, emotional range, intonation, impressions, speed, tone and whispering
systems.languages_note: Optimised for English; no language table published
systems.runs_on: Cloud only
systems.best_for: Directable delivery without SSML, with the safest data posture available — no training by default, zero-retention for approved customers, and HIPAA BAAs.
systems.watch: Three separate ways to get speech out of OpenAI with three different price structures; choosing wrongly is a 4× cost error. Snapshot churn is real — one TTS snapshot was retired in July 2026.

systems.name: IBM Watson TTS
systems.cloning: Custom branded neural voice from ~1 hour of recordings (Premium)
systems.emotion: SSML with IBM extensions; voice transformation for breathiness, pitch, timbre; IPA or IBM SPR
systems.runs_on: Cloud, Cloud Pak on-prem, and an embeddable containerised library licensable to ISVs
systems.latency_note: Expressive voices documented as slightly higher; no absolute figure
systems.best_for: Regulated enterprises needing genuinely portable on-prem or hybrid TTS and a redistributable embed licence — the strongest OEM story of any vendor here.
systems.watch: Smallest language footprint of any major vendor, at a price above Azure and Polly Neural. Its differentiation is deployment portability, not breadth.

systems.name: Alibaba Qwen3-TTS
systems.cloning: $0.01 per clone with 1,000 free, then $11.50 / 1M chars
systems.emotion: Natural-language instruction control on the -instruct models
systems.languages_note: Mandarin plus ~21 dialects, and 12 other languages
systems.runs_on: Cloud — separate Singapore and Beijing deployments
systems.best_for: The price leader that no comparison table names. Cheaper than Azure standard neural while being an LLM-era model, with by far the deepest Chinese-dialect coverage anywhere.
systems.watch: Two pricing regimes with materially different rates for the same model, free quotas that expire after 90 days, and a compliance posture Western enterprises must diligence separately.

systems.name: Anthropic
systems.best_for: Nothing in this segment. Pair the Claude API with a third-party TTS, or run Claude on Bedrock or Vertex alongside Polly or Chirp.
systems.watch: Verified, not assumed — neither the models overview nor the API overview contains any occurrence of TTS, text-to-speech, audio, speech or voice as a product capability. A complete gap versus every other frontier lab.

systems.name: Meta
systems.cloning: Not a product capability; Voicebox was never released
systems.emotion: Expression transfer through translation, not authored control
systems.languages_note: ~100 in / 36 out for S2S; MMS covers ~1,100
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted GPU; Meta operates no TTS API
systems.latency_note: ~2 s for streaming translation, not TTS
systems.best_for: Speech-to-speech translation research and long-tail language coverage via MMS.
systems.watch: Meta has shipped nothing in speech since December 2023 — every 2025–26 release from the facebook org is vision, 3D or robotics. CC-BY-NC prohibits commercial use outright; this is a hard block, not a "verify first".

systems.name: VoxCPM2
systems.cloning: Zero-shot, reference+transcript mode, AND voice design from text with no reference at all
systems.emotion: Natural-language voice design plus style steering
systems.languages_note: 30 plus Chinese dialects, with automatic detection
systems.runs_on: GPU, ~8 GB VRAM
systems.latency_note: RTF 0.30 on an RTX 4090; 0.13 with Nano-vLLM
systems.best_for: The strongest genuinely commercial-usable open model of 2026 — native 48 kHz with no external upsampler, 1.0 M downloads a month.
systems.watch: The 8 GB VRAM floor rules out CPU and most edge deployment, and no ONNX or GGUF export is documented.

systems.name: Qwen3-TTS
systems.emotion: Natural-language voice design, plus instruction control over 9 preset timbres
systems.runs_on: GPU; the 0.6 B variant is the small-footprint option
systems.latency_note: 97 ms claimed, with no hardware stated
systems.best_for: Commercial realtime voice agents at the 1–2 B scale — Apache-2.0, 3-second cloning and streaming from a single model.
systems.watch: Alibaba has since pivoted its flagship audio models to a closed API, so long-term open support is uncertain.

systems.name: MOSS-TTS
systems.cloning: Zero-shot; v1.5 targets similarity variance and long-reference/short-text
systems.emotion: Punctuation-driven prosody, explicit pause markers, token-level duration control, Pinyin and IPA
systems.runs_on: 8 B needs a datacentre GPU; the 0.1 B Nano runs realtime on a single CPU core
systems.latency_note: 180 ms TTFB with RTF 0.51 (Realtime variant), no hardware stated
systems.best_for: Covering the whole size range from one family, with native 48 kHz STEREO output — essentially unique among open TTS.
systems.watch: Release-date documentation is inconsistent across the repo, paper and community trackers, and the family naming is confusing.

systems.name: dots.tts
systems.cloning: Continuation cloning from reference audio plus transcript
systems.emotion: Implicit from the reference only
systems.runs_on: GPU; VRAM not published
systems.best_for: Speaker similarity as the top priority — the highest average across 24 languages of any open model, with no codec bottleneck at 48 kHz.
systems.watch: Very low adoption, so few community integrations and little third-party validation. Low-resource languages show notably higher error rates.

systems.name: LongCat-AudioDiT
systems.cloning: Zero-shot — the best published speaker-similarity scores of any open model
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: GPU; VRAM not published
systems.best_for: Maximum clone fidelity with genuinely clean licensing — diffusion directly in waveform latent space, no mel intermediate.
systems.watch: Holds the best similarity scores in the open ecosystem and gets roughly a thousandth of XTTS-v2's downloads. Adoption tracks tooling, not benchmarks.

systems.name: Chatterbox
systems.emotion: Continuous exaggeration parameter plus CFG weight; Turbo and Nano add inline paralinguistic tags
systems.runs_on: CUDA, CPU and Apple MPS; Nano runs at 3× realtime on 8 CPU cores
systems.latency_note: 75 ms and 6× realtime claimed for Turbo, with no GPU named
systems.best_for: The only major open model shipping neural watermarking by default — the single best answer to the EU AI Act marking duty if you self-host.
systems.watch: The watermark is a property of the official repository, not the weights; an MIT fork can strip the call in one line, and forks that do exist.

systems.name: Fish Audio S2 Pro
systems.emotion: 15,000+ free-form inline natural-language tags — the most controllable open TTS shipped
systems.runs_on: GPU, ~10 GB class
systems.latency_note: RTF 0.195 and ~100 ms TTFA on an H200 — one of the few models publishing hardware
systems.best_for: Research and evaluation. Best Seed-TTS-eval error rates of any open model, at 0.54% Chinese CER and 0.99% English WER.
systems.watch: Routinely reported as MIT. It is not — commercial use requires a separate paid licence, and Fish's own blog says "open weights, not open source by the OSI definition".

systems.name: Higgs Audio v3
systems.licence: Research + Creator Use Grant with attribution
systems.price_note: Free for research and credited creator use
systems.cloning: Zero-shot; supplying a reference transcript materially improves fidelity
systems.emotion: 21 discrete emotion tokens, insertable mid-utterance
systems.runs_on: GPU; VRAM not published
systems.best_for: The broadest language coverage of any open model, with genuine inline emotion control.
systems.watch: Production, hosted APIs and revenue-generating deployment all require a separate commercial licence. The Creator Use Grant is unusual and requires crediting Boson AI.

systems.name: IndexTTS
systems.price_note: Free below the MAU and revenue thresholds
systems.cloning: Zero-shot with speaker identity DISENTANGLED from emotion
systems.emotion: Best-in-class — 8 emotion dimensions controlled three ways (separate reference audio, 0–1 intensity vectors, or free text), plus explicit duration control
systems.runs_on: GPU
systems.latency_note: 2.5 claims a 2.28× improvement over 2, with no absolute figure
systems.best_for: Emotion- and duration-controlled dubbing and localisation, where separating who is speaking from how they feel is the whole job.
systems.watch: Widely reported as Apache-2.0. It is not — the licence carries MAU and revenue thresholds, prohibited-use clauses covering medical, military and biometric surveillance, a bar on improving other commercial AI models, and PRC governing law.

systems.name: Step-Audio-EditX
systems.emotion: The most complete editing surface in open TTS — 14 emotions, 30+ speaking styles, 10 paralinguistic tag types, and iterative re-editing of already-generated audio
systems.runs_on: 12 GB VRAM, or 6–8 GB with the official AWQ 4-bit build
systems.best_for: Post-hoc emotion and style editing of existing audio — the only open model doing true iterative editing well.
systems.watch: Hard 30-second limit per inference, and no streaming.

systems.name: VibeVoice
systems.licence: MIT, with usage restrictions layered on in the model card
systems.cloning: Yes, via speaker prompts — the capability that triggered the takedown
systems.emotion: Implicit from context
systems.runs_on: GPU; VRAM not published
systems.best_for: Long-form multi-speaker generation — 90 minutes with 4 distinct speakers in a single pass, an outlier by more than an order of magnitude.
systems.watch: Microsoft removed the TTS code from the official repo two weeks after release citing misuse. The weights remain and community forks maintain the code, but upstream continuity is a real risk.

systems.name: ZONOS2
systems.licence: MIT or Apache-2.0 — the repo and product page disagree
systems.cloning: Zero-shot via a new ECAPA-TDNN speaker embedder; expressive and stable modes
systems.emotion: Additive emotion direction vectors plus valence and arousal sliders — the richest continuous emotion API in open TTS
systems.languages_note: 30+ across three tiers, with native code-switching
systems.runs_on: GPU; 8 B total parameters must be resident despite 900 M active
systems.latency_note: 4× throughput over its predecessor, no absolute figure
systems.best_for: Permissively-licensed multilingual cloning with genuine continuous emotion control. The only sparse mixture-of-experts TTS in the open ecosystem.
systems.watch: Resolve the licence discrepancy against the repository's LICENSE file before commercial reliance. Byte-level input removes the phonemizer dependency entirely, which also sidesteps the eSpeak GPL question.

systems.name: Fun-CosyVoice 3.0
systems.emotion: Instruction-based, plus pronunciation control via Pinyin and CMU phoneme inpainting
systems.runs_on: GPU; 0.5 B is modest
systems.latency_note: 150 ms with bi-streaming, no hardware stated
systems.best_for: Chinese-first commercial products needing dialect coverage and bidirectional streaming at only 0.5 B parameters.
systems.watch: The repository naming across CosyVoice2 and Fun-CosyVoice3 is confusing, and adoption is lower than its quality warrants.

systems.name: Voxtral TTS
systems.price_note: Free for research; hosted API $16 / 1M chars
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from as little as 3 s, with cross-lingual accent preservation
systems.emotion: Expressive but with no documented explicit parameter
systems.runs_on: GPU; a Q4_K GGUF build is ~7.43 GB
systems.latency_note: 70 ms for a typical prompt, no hardware stated
systems.best_for: Non-commercial European-language voice work, and evaluation before buying the commercial licence. The first major European lab open-weights TTS.
systems.watch: A hard 2-minute native generation ceiling. Mistral's hosted API papers over it with interleaving; self-hosting does not.

systems.name: OmniVoice
systems.emotion: Voice design by attribute — gender, age, pitch, dialect, whisper, accent — stable mainly for Chinese and English
systems.languages_note: 600+ — the broadest of any zero-shot TTS by a wide margin
systems.runs_on: GPU; RTF 0.0115 at batch 8 on an H100
systems.latency_note: RTF 0.025 single-request, 0.0115 batched on an H100
systems.best_for: Low-resource language coverage and extremely fast batched inference. 862 k downloads a month within four months of release.
systems.watch: The Apache-2.0 code licence does not extend to the weights, which are CC-BY-NC. This catches people out constantly.

systems.name: GPT-SoVITS
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from 5 s, and few-shot FINE-TUNING from one minute of audio
systems.emotion: Via reference-clip selection
systems.runs_on: CUDA, Apple Silicon and CPU — RTF 0.014 on a 4090, 0.526 on an M4 CPU
systems.latency_note: RTF 0.014 (RTX 4090) · 0.028 (4060 Ti) · 0.526 (M4 CPU) — a rare per-device table
systems.best_for: Fine-tuning one specific character voice from about a minute of data, with the best fine-tuning ergonomics in open TTS.
systems.watch: No tagged release since June 2025, and despite frequent references there is no v5.

systems.name: F5-TTS
systems.cloning: Zero-shot, but the reference transcript is required
systems.emotion: None
systems.languages_note: 2 official, with a large community ecosystem
systems.runs_on: GPU; CPU slowly; ROCm support added in 2026
systems.latency_note: RTF ~0.15 on an RTX 4090, commonly cited
systems.best_for: Retraining on your own licensed data — the most-forked TTS architecture of the era and the base of much of the fine-tuning tooling ecosystem.
systems.watch: Reported as MIT almost everywhere. The code is MIT; the released checkpoints are CC-BY-NC because of the Emilia training corpus, so commercial use requires retraining.

systems.name: XTTS-v2
systems.licence: Weights CPML — non-commercial. Fork code is MPL-2.0.
systems.emotion: Transferred from the reference clip
systems.runs_on: GPU ~4 GB fp16, and CPU
systems.best_for: Legacy compatibility and the widest single-toolkit model catalogue.
systems.watch: A December 2023 model still pulling 9.16 M downloads a month. CPML restricts commercial use of both the model AND the generated audio — the most commonly misreported licence in the segment.

systems.name: MegaTTS 3
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 in name only — the encoder is withheld
systems.cloning: Effectively impossible — you cannot encode your own reference audio
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: GPU
systems.best_for: Little, practically. Included as the clearest example of nominal versus effective openness.
systems.watch: ByteDance withholds the WaveVAE encoder weights "for security issues", so inference only runs from latents ByteDance provides. No update since March 2025.

systems.name: Orpheus TTS
systems.emotion: Inline emotion and intonation tags
systems.languages_note: English primary, plus 7 research language pairs
systems.runs_on: GPU, 3 B class
systems.latency_note: ~200 ms streaming, ~100 ms with input streaming, no hardware stated
systems.best_for: Apache-2.0 realtime English agents where a large hosted-inference ecosystem matters more than cutting-edge quality.
systems.watch: No 2026 GitHub releases and 118 open issues; the promised 1B, 400M and 150M variants never shipped despite appearing in comparison tables. Activity moved entirely to hosted inference.

systems.name: Dia / Dia2
systems.emotion: Non-verbal tags inline
systems.runs_on: RTX 4090 measured at ~4.4 GB bf16, 2.1× realtime with torch.compile
systems.best_for: English two-speaker dialogue and podcast generation at low VRAM.
systems.watch: No 2026 release. The team self-describes as one full-time and one part-time engineer, and a waitlist for larger models suggests the best ones will not be open.

systems.name: ZipVoice
systems.cloning: Zero-shot; reference clips under 3 s recommended
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: GPU and CPU ONNX int8 — but explicitly not ONNX on GPU
systems.best_for: The smallest model achieving competitive similarity at 123 M parameters, with a genuinely rare stereo dialogue variant that puts one speaker per channel.
systems.watch: The k2-fsa team's attention has clearly moved to OmniVoice; no 2026 release.

systems.name: Sesame CSM-1B
systems.cloning: Context-conditioned, not a conventional zero-shot interface
systems.emotion: Implicit from conversational context — the architectural selling point
systems.runs_on: GPU, ~1 B class
systems.best_for: Research into context-aware conversational speech, and as a base architecture — Marvis-TTS and others are built on it.
systems.watch: Frozen since March 2025. The viral Maya demo used larger internal models that were never released, so demo quality is not what you get.

systems.name: OuteTTS 1.0
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: llama.cpp, vLLM, ExLlamaV2, and CPU via GGUF
systems.best_for: Running TTS inside an existing llama.cpp or vLLM stack — as a pure language model it inherits the entire quantisation ecosystem for free.
systems.watch: Frequently listed as Apache-2.0. The model card's own front-matter says CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, which is non-commercial and imposes share-alike on derivatives.

systems.name: Parler-TTS
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 — datasets, training code AND weights
systems.emotion: Free-form natural-language description of speaker characteristics
systems.runs_on: GPU and CPU
systems.best_for: Fully auditable training pipelines. Historically important for pioneering the description-conditioned mechanism that Maya1, Qwen3-VoiceDesign and VoxCPM2 now use.
systems.watch: Dormant since August 2024 and well behind 2026 quality. Use it as a reference implementation, not in production.

systems.name: StyleTTS 2
systems.licence: Code MIT; pretrained models add a synthetic-disclosure duty
systems.emotion: Style vectors sampled via diffusion
systems.runs_on: GPU and CPU
systems.latency_note: Faster than realtime; no canonical figure
systems.best_for: Understanding or forking the architecture that underlies Kokoro.
systems.watch: Effectively unmaintained since 2024, and superseded by its own derivative. The pretrained-model condition requiring you to inform listeners the speech is synthetic is non-standard.

systems.name: Piper
systems.cloning: No cloning, but you can train new voices
systems.emotion: None — speed and noise variation only
systems.runs_on: CPU on x86 and ARM, Raspberry Pi 3/4/5, embedded; also via sherpa-onnx on Android, iOS and RISC-V
systems.latency_note: 0.54× core-hour ratio on a Ryzen 7 5700X (Picovoice, July 2026)
systems.best_for: The default and safest choice for offline neural TTS on Pi-class hardware, and the Home Assistant default. Best language breadth among tiny engines.
systems.watch: Relicensed from MIT to GPL-3.0; the MIT-era repository is archived read-only. Anyone who embedded old Piper in a proprietary product cannot simply upgrade.

systems.name: Supertonic 3
systems.cloning: Advertised for Supertonic 3, unconfirmed in the README
systems.emotion: 10 inline expression tags
systems.runs_on: CPU via ONNX, browser via WebGPU, servers, Raspberry Pi, even e-readers
systems.latency_note: RTF 0.012–0.015 on an M4 Pro; RTF ~0.3 on a Raspberry Pi
systems.best_for: The fastest genuinely-good on-device TTS available as open weights, at 44.1 kHz with 31 languages and no GPU required.
systems.watch: OpenRAIL-M is not an OSI licence and carries use-based restrictions that some legal teams reject. Streaming is not documented.

systems.name: Kyutai pocket-tts
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: CPU; a Core ML port targets Apple Silicon
systems.latency_note: ~200 ms to first audio and ~6× realtime on a MacBook Air M4 using only 2 CPU cores
systems.best_for: True 80 ms frame streaming on-device — one of the two current state-of-the-art options for speed-at-quality on a laptop.
systems.watch: The Core ML English pack is 766 MB at fp16. Only part of the pipeline runs on the Neural Engine; the language model falls back to GPU.

systems.name: Kokoro-82M
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: CPU, CUDA, Apple Silicon, browser via WASM and WebGPU, sherpa-onnx, MLX
systems.latency_note: 1.4× core-hour ratio — SLOWER than realtime on one core (Picovoice, July 2026)
systems.best_for: Best naturalness-per-megabyte for offline synthesis, and the default pick for browser-side TTS. 11.3 M downloads a month.
systems.watch: Frozen since January 2025 with no successor, no cloning and no emotion control. That download figure is momentum, not currency — and it is not really a Raspberry-Pi-class model.

systems.name: NeuTTS Air
systems.licence: Air is Apache-2.0; Nano and 2E use a custom NeuTTS Open License
systems.cloning: Instant from ~3 s of reference audio
systems.emotion: 2E adds 6 emotions plus neutral; Air and Nano have none
systems.runs_on: CPU via llama.cpp GGUF — 20–45 tok/s on a Galaxy A25 phone, 111–195 on an iMac M4
systems.latency_note: Throughput published per device; first-audio latency is not
systems.best_for: The closest thing to a local ElevenLabs workflow — instant voice cloning that fits on a laptop CPU or a mid-range phone, with true token-level streaming.
systems.watch: A hard ~30-second generation ceiling from the 2,048-token context, and the reference audio counts against it. Ships Perth watermarking by default.

systems.name: MOSS-TTS-Nano
systems.emotion: Punctuation-driven prosody and pause markers
systems.runs_on: Realtime on a SINGLE CPU core on a MacBook Air M4 via ONNX; no GPU required
systems.latency_note: Realtime on one CPU core; no RTF table published
systems.best_for: The best CPU-only option that still has multilingual coverage and voice cloning, at 48 kHz stereo from 0.1 B parameters.
systems.watch: Quality at 0.1 B will not match 1 B+ models, and the project is young with limited third-party validation.

systems.name: KittenTTS
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: CPU only; the int8 Nano is 25 MB total
systems.latency_note: 5.1× SLOWER than realtime on a Ryzen 7 5700X (Picovoice, July 2026)
systems.best_for: The smallest credible neural TTS binary in wide use, for IoT and anywhere 25 MB is the hard budget.
systems.watch: Small does not mean fast — the 25 MB darling of every roundup measured among the slowest engines tested. Known failures on numerals; pre-expand numbers to words.

systems.name: Marvis-TTS
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: Apple Silicon first-class via MLX; ~500 MB quantised
systems.latency_note: Streaming as text arrives; no numeric RTF published
systems.best_for: The best-integrated Apple Silicon and iOS on-device TTS with voice cloning.
systems.watch: Only three languages, no emotion control, and disk-size figures conflict badly between the model card and the launch blog.

systems.name: Picovoice Orca
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: CPU and embedded — 7 MB model, 29 MB peak memory
systems.latency_note: 128 ms first-token-to-speech, 0.16× core-hour ratio on a Ryzen 7 5700X
systems.best_for: The only on-device engine that consumes an LLM token stream directly — genuine streaming input, which Android's own API cannot do.
systems.watch: The benchmark establishing these figures is authored by Picovoice, and Orca wins it. The methodology is transparent, but read the framing critically.

systems.name: Apple Personal Voice
systems.cloning: 10 prompts in under a minute on iOS 26, fully on-device
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: iOS and macOS, entirely on-device
systems.best_for: The only consumer-grade on-device voice banking, exposed to apps through the standard speech-synthesis API.
systems.watch: No supported export path to third-party AAC hardware, which is exactly where a banked voice is most needed. Beta reports of English voices silently switching language and breaking.

systems.name: Android TextToSpeech
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: Android
systems.best_for: Baseline accessibility and read-aloud on Android with zero dependencies.
systems.watch: Requires the COMPLETE utterance before synthesis — it cannot consume a token stream, which is a structural blocker for LLM voice agents. And Gemini Nano does NOT provide on-device TTS; its audio tasks are recognition, not generation.

systems.name: Web Speech API
systems.emotion: SSML is ignored by most implementations
systems.runs_on: Most browsers — but NOT Opera Android or Android WebView, which breaks Cordova and Capacitor apps
systems.best_for: Quick wins where a rough read-aloud with no dependencies is enough.
systems.watch: A compatibility shim, not an engine. Chrome truncates past ~200–250 characters, background tabs are throttled, and SOME BROWSER VOICES ARE CLOUD VOICES — the text leaves the device, defeating the point for privacy-sensitive apps.

systems.name: OpenAI Realtime
systems.emotion: Implicit from the conversation and session instructions
systems.runs_on: Cloud, over WebRTC or WebSocket
systems.best_for: Latency-sensitive agents where the model should hear tone rather than a transcript, and where WebRTC browser delivery matters.
systems.watch: Cached audio input is $0.40 per 1M against $32 fresh — an ~80× reduction, so any cost comparison ignoring prompt caching overstates by multiples. The voice cannot be changed once a session has emitted audio.

systems.name: Google Gemini Live
systems.emotion: Implicit, with acoustic-nuance detection
systems.runs_on: Cloud, bidirectional WebSocket
systems.best_for: Roughly an order of magnitude cheaper per audio token than OpenAI Realtime, and unusually transparent in publishing both per-token and per-minute rates.
systems.watch: All the Live models are Preview and subject to change. The newer 3.1 dropped the non-blocking function calling that lets an agent keep talking while a tool runs.

systems.name: Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
systems.emotion: Adapts delivery to the prosody of your input speech
systems.runs_on: Cloud, Bedrock event-driven bidirectional stream
systems.best_for: AWS-native agents needing graceful interruption, background-noise robustness and asynchronous tool calling in one model.
systems.watch: Nova Sonic v1 has a hard end-of-life of 14 September 2026. v2 is ~12% cheaper on speech but 5.5× dearer on text input and 11× on text output, which penalises tool-heavy agents.

systems.name: Moshi
systems.emotion: Natural backchannels from conversational training
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted GPU
systems.latency_note: 160 ms theoretical, ~200 ms measured on an L4
systems.best_for: Genuine full-duplex conversation — simultaneous listening and speaking, not merely barge-in. The foundation of the Mimi codec lineage.
systems.watch: No tool calling at all, which is the biggest functional gap of the open full-duplex models versus hosted APIs.

systems.name: NVIDIA PersonaPlex
systems.licence: MIT code, NVIDIA Open Model weights
systems.emotion: Natural, including genuine backchanneling while the user is still speaking
systems.runs_on: ~8 GB VRAM per hands-on reports; a CPU-offload flag exists
systems.best_for: The best open full-duplex conversational feel, and the only open model evaluated on backchanneling.
systems.watch: No tool calling. Latency and VRAM figures circulate widely but are not stated in the repository itself.

systems.name: MiniCPM-o 4.5
systems.emotion: Natural
systems.runs_on: 11 GB INT4 or 19 GB BF16; runs full-duplex on a 16 GB M3 Mac and supports phone deployment
systems.best_for: Full omni-modal understanding and generation WITH voice cloning, self-hosted at a genuinely reachable VRAM floor.
systems.watch: Dynamic mid-conversation context injection is untested, and zero-shot cloning will not match a fine-tuned voice.

systems.name: Step-Audio 2
systems.emotion: Yes
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted GPU
systems.best_for: Almost uniquely among open speech-to-speech models, it ships first-class tool calling — with its own benchmark for it.
systems.watch: Barge-in rather than genuine full-duplex.

systems.name: Ultravox
systems.emotion: Not applicable
systems.runs_on: Cloud or self-host
systems.best_for: Replacing STT and the LLM in one model while keeping full control of the voice.
systems.watch: This is SPEECH-IN, TEXT-OUT — you still need a separate TTS stage. It is very commonly miscategorised as speech-to-speech.

systems.name: RVC / Applio
systems.cloning: Per-speaker training from ~10 minutes of audio, in 10–30 minutes
systems.emotion: Excellent — preserves the F0 contour, so pitch, sarcasm, whispering and emphasis all survive conversion
systems.runs_on: 2–4 GB VRAM
systems.best_for: The community standard. Stack it after any TTS for a similarity boost of roughly 0.03–0.08 — usually a bigger gain than switching TTS models.
systems.watch: Requires per-speaker training rather than zero-shot, so it is a pipeline step, not a drop-in.

systems.name: Seed-VC v2
systems.emotion: Good; converts accent and emotion
systems.runs_on: 4–8 GB VRAM
systems.best_for: The best published zero-shot voice-conversion quality.
systems.watch: 300–400 ms of added latency is borderline for a sub-500 ms conversational budget, and GPL-3.0 matters for products.

systems.name: Azure Voice Conversion
systems.emotion: Carried from the source speech
systems.runs_on: Cloud
systems.best_for: The only hyperscaler pricing standalone timbre transfer as a product.
systems.watch: Requires a custom voice, which is itself Limited Access.

systems.name: OpenVoice v2
systems.emotion: Tone colour only
systems.runs_on: ~2 GB
systems.best_for: The simplest permissively-licensed option.
systems.watch: Converts tone colour rather than full voice identity — expect noticeably less than RVC.

systems.name: MeanVC
systems.emotion: Unknown — the recognition stage may strip nuance
systems.runs_on: Under 1 GB at 14 M parameters
systems.best_for: The smallest streaming-capable voice conversion, single-step and genuinely fast.
systems.watch: Very new, with little independent validation.

systems.name: eSpeak NG
systems.emotion: Pitch, rate and variant only
systems.runs_on: Essentially anything — Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, RISC-V, WASM, microcontroller-class
systems.latency_note: Effectively instantaneous; orders of magnitude faster than realtime
systems.best_for: Screen readers at 400–800 words per minute, where latency and rate-scalability beat naturalness completely. Also the phonemizer inside Piper, Kokoro, StyleTTS 2 and much of this table.
systems.watch: A transitive GPL-3.0 exposure nobody discusses — products shipping Piper or Kokoro should check whether they are linking GPL code.

systems.name: Flite / Festival
systems.cloning: None — but FestVox builds voices from recordings
systems.emotion: None
systems.runs_on: Very small embedded systems upward; under 1 MB runtime memory
systems.best_for: Hard-constrained embedded systems with no ML runtime, deterministic memory budgets and genuinely permissive licensing.
systems.watch: In maintenance mode, and audibly dated.

systems.name: ETI-Eloquence
systems.emotion: Pitch and rate
systems.runs_on: Windows, inside screen readers
systems.best_for: Still shipping in JAWS 2026 and still winning on merit at 800 words per minute — the clearest evidence that naturalness is not the objective function in accessibility.
systems.watch: A 1990s formant synthesiser. It sounds like one, and its users do not care.

systems.name: VITS / Matcha / Glow-TTS
systems.emotion: None
systems.languages_note: Piper covers 30+; the Fairseq VITS collection covers ~1,100
systems.runs_on: CPU-viable at RTF under 0.1; ONNX exports standard; Raspberry Pi class
systems.latency_note: Well under RTF 0.1 on modest CPU
systems.best_for: The actual workhorses of production offline TTS — every Home Assistant install, every accessibility tool, every embedded product. Boring, tiny, permissive and reliable.
systems.watch: No cloning, no emotion, and per-voice models must be trained individually.

corrections.claim: Azure standard neural TTS is $16 per 1M characters
corrections.reality: $15.00, consistently across 35 commercial regions per the retail price API, and $18.75 in Azure Government.

corrections.claim: Azure Neural HD is $30 per 1M characters
corrections.reality: $22.00 since March 2026 — which makes Azure HD cheaper than Google Chirp 3 HD and Amazon Polly Generative.

corrections.claim: Fish Audio S2 Pro is MIT-licensed
corrections.reality: It is the Fish Audio Research License, which is non-commercial. Fish's own blog says "open weights, not open source by the OSI definition".

corrections.claim: IndexTTS 2 is Apache-2.0
corrections.reality: A custom bilibili Model Use License with MAU and revenue thresholds, prohibited-use clauses, and PRC governing law.

corrections.claim: F5-TTS is MIT
corrections.reality: The code is MIT; the released checkpoints are CC-BY-NC because of the Emilia training corpus.

corrections.claim: OuteTTS is Apache-2.0
corrections.reality: The model card's own front-matter says CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 — non-commercial and share-alike.

corrections.claim: Piper is MIT-licensed
corrections.reality: GPL-3.0 since v1.3.0. The MIT-era repository has been archived read-only since October 2025.

corrections.claim: MegaTTS 3 is Apache-2.0 and does voice cloning
corrections.reality: Apache-2.0 in name only — the WaveVAE encoder is withheld, so you cannot encode your own reference audio.

corrections.claim: PlayHT is a leading TTS vendor
corrections.reality: Permanently shut down on 31 December 2025. All customer voice clones were deleted with no export path.

corrections.claim: Replica Studios is the SAG-AFTRA-approved AI voice vendor
corrections.reality: Ceased operations. Its site serves a farewell notice and its pricing page returns 404.

corrections.claim: Papercup competes with ElevenLabs on dubbing
corrections.reality: Acquired — papercup.com now redirects to RWS.

corrections.claim: VocaliD is a voice-banking option
corrections.reality: Absorbed — vocalid.ai redirects to Veritone Voice, with no mention of the brand.

corrections.claim: ACX accepts AI narration
corrections.reality: ACX's own requirements state unauthorised text-to-speech is prohibited. The only sanctioned paths are Amazon Virtual Voice and an invite-only ACX beta.

corrections.claim: Gemini Nano will handle on-device TTS on Android
corrections.reality: It will not. The on-device audio tasks are speech RECOGNITION, not generation.

corrections.claim: KittenTTS is fast because it is only 25 MB
corrections.reality: An open benchmark measured it at 5.1× slower than realtime — among the slowest engines tested.

corrections.claim: Lower word error rate means better TTS
corrections.reality: WER correlates NEGATIVELY with perceived quality across ~11,800 human ratings. Over-articulated, flat, recogniser-friendly speech scores well and sounds bad.

corrections.claim: Freeze-Omni and VITA-Audio are open source
corrections.reality: Both carry custom academic and research-only licences prohibiting commercial use.

corrections.claim: The EU AI Act was delayed
corrections.reality: Only the high-risk deadlines moved. Article 50 transparency applied from 2 August 2026 as originally scheduled.

corrections.claim: The NO FAKES Act is law
corrections.reality: It cleared Senate Judiciary in June 2026 but has passed neither chamber. Treat "NO FAKES compliant" as marketing.

corrections.claim: Anthropic has a TTS API
corrections.reality: It has no TTS, no speech-to-speech model and no audio output modality of any kind.

gaps: Data retention and training-on-your-data policy could not be verified from primary sources for most vendors. TTS inputs routinely contain personal data — get these terms contractually.

Tencent, Baidu and Yandex pricing is unverifiable from English-language primary sources. Tencent publishes no rate and its billing docs 404; Baidu's pricing page returns empty content; Yandex's docs sit behind a bot-check.
MiniMax Speech 2.6 pricing is reported at $60–100 per million characters by third parties, and no MiniMax-owned page would confirm it. It is therefore omitted rather than published as fact.
Amazon Nova 2 Sonic language coverage, voice list, latency and regional availability could not be reached. Do not assume it inherits v1's five-language list.
Latency for almost every hyperscaler is simply not published. Microsoft is the only one stating a concrete figure, so every latency comparison in that segment rests on third-party measurement.
Essentially no vendor publishes quality metrics — MOS, UTMOS, WER or arena rating — for its 2026 voice sets.
Per-service compliance certifications (HIPAA BAA eligibility, FedRAMP level, GDPR DPA specifics) were not verified per TTS product. Regulated procurement must confirm directly.
No watermark robustness figure in circulation is a verified benchmark. Vendor accuracy claims for audio watermarking do not appear in the corresponding repositories.
Several licences remain genuinely ambiguous — ZONOS2, GLM-TTS weights, NeuTTS Nano, MaskGCT checkpoints, and KaniTTS's three stacked licences.
